business_model.claim: Trinity Industries, Inc. provides railcar leasing and management, railcar manufacturing, railcar maintenance and modifications, and other railcar logistics products and services in North America under the TrinityRail® trade name, alongside RSI Logistics software and logistics solutions and Holden America railcar parts and components.
quotes: Trinity Industries, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries (“Trinity,” “Company,” “we,” “our,” or “us”) own businesses that are leading providers of railcar products and services in North America.
We market our railcar products and services under the trade name TrinityRail®.
Our platform also includes the brands of RSI Logistics, a provider of software and logistics solutions, and Holden America, a supplier of railcar parts and components.
Our platform provides railcar leasing and management services; railcar manufacturing; railcar maintenance and modifications; and other railcar logistics products and services.

business_model.claim: Trinity sells and leases its railcars, parts, and services primarily through its own sales personnel across the U.S., Canada, and Mexico to railroads, industrial shippers, and third-party leasing companies operating in refined products and chemicals, energy, agriculture, construction and metals, and consumer products.
quotes: The TrinityRail platform serves as a single point of contact for railroads, shippers, and third-party leasing companies seeking rail equipment and services.
These companies operate in various markets, including refined products and chemicals, energy, agriculture, construction and metals, and consumer products.
We sell or lease substantially all of our products and services through our own sales personnel operating from offices in multiple U.S. locations, as well as Canada and Mexico.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P4
business_model.claim: Trinity reports its operating results in two reportable segments: the Railcar Leasing and Services Group and the Rail Products Group.
quotes: We report our operating results in two reportable segments: (1) the Railcar Leasing and Services Group (the "Leasing Group"), which owns and operates a fleet of railcars and provides third-party fleet leasing, management, and administrative services; railcar maintenance and modification services; and other railcar logistics products and services; and (2) the Rail Products Group, which manufactures and sells railcars and related parts and components.

business_model.claim: The Leasing Group earns recurring revenue predominantly from full-service operating leases with fixed monthly rentals varying from one year to ten years (alongside smaller per diem variable and net leases), plus fee income from managing third-party investor-owned fleets and external maintenance, modification, and digital logistics services.
quotes: The terms of our railcar leases generally provide for fixed monthly rentals that vary from one year to ten years.

We serve our customers predominantly through full-service leases; however, a small portion of our lease fleet operates on per diem leases that earn usage-based variable lease payments or on net leases under which the lessee assumes responsibility for maintenance of the railcars.

Our affiliations with third-party investor-owned funds, through strategic railcar alliances and the formation of railcar investment vehicles, combined with TILC's fleet maintenance and management services capabilities, complement our leasing business by generating stable fee income, strengthening customer relationships, and enhancing the view of TrinityRail as a leading provider of railcar products and services.

business_model.claim: In full-year 2025, the Leasing Group generated $1,206.6 (table in millions) in total revenue—$919.1 in leasing and management, 247.4 in maintenance services, and 40.1 in digital and logistics services—and $708.4 in operating profit, while Leasing & Services revenue was 851.9 (table in millions) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
quotes: Total revenues for the Railcar Leasing and Services Group increased by 5.5% for the year ended December 31, 2025 when compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: The Rail Products Group manufactures freight and tank railcars in U.S. and Mexico facilities, performs sustainable railcar conversions, and supplies parts and components both to external buyers and internally to build the Leasing Group's fleet.
quotes: Through wholly-owned subsidiaries with facilities in the U.S. and Mexico, our Rail Products Group is a leading manufacturer of freight and tank railcars in North America used for transporting a wide variety of liquids, gases, and dry cargo.
Additionally, our Rail Products Group offers a sustainable railcar conversion program whereby certain tank cars and freight cars are converted or upgraded to better meet changing market demands.
Substantially all of the railcars in our lease fleet were manufactured by our Rail Products Group.

business_model.claim: Material inputs—principally steel and specialty components such as brakes, wheels, heads, side frames, bolsters, and bearings—represent on average more than 70% of the cost of most railcars, making manufacturing costs sensitive to input price volatility and supplier availability.
quotes: The input costs for materials, including raw steel, specialty components, and other parts and coatings purchased from third parties, represent, on average, more than 70% of the cost of most railcars.

We typically use contract-specific purchasing practices, existing supplier commitments, contractual price escalation provisions, and other arrangements with our customers to reduce the impact of plate and coil steel price volatility on our operating profit.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, P4, and P5
business_model.claim: Manufacturing costs and margins are also moved by production volume overhead absorption, skilled labor availability (such as welders), and cross-border U.S.–Mexico risks—including tariffs, duties, and rail border disruptions at Eagle Pass, Texas—because the majority of railcars are manufactured in Mexico.
quotes: The majority of our railcars are manufactured in Mexico.
Tariffs, duties, or related cash deposit requirements could increase costs, disrupt our integrated U.S.-Mexico manufacturing operations, and adversely affect our results of operations and cash flows.

We have, from time to time, been impacted by disruptions in the rail transportation network, including rail traffic closures or congestion in Eagle Pass, Texas, the primary border crossing used for railcar deliveries from our manufacturing facilities in Mexico.

quotes: TRL-2023 Term Loan – In April 2025, Trinity Rail Leasing 2023 LLC (“TRL-2023”), a limited purpose, indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company owned through Trinity Industries Leasing Company (“TILC”), entered into an amended and restated term loan agreement to (i) increase the aggregate amount of the term loan from $320.7 million as of March 31, 2025 to $1.05 billion; (ii) extend the maturity date to April 30, 2030; and (iii) reduce the applicable interest rate to daily simple SOFR plus a facility margin of 1.50%.

In October 2025, Trinity Rail Leasing 2025 LLC ("TRL-2025"), a limited purpose, indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company owned through TILC, issued an aggregate principal amount of $535.2 million of its Series 2025-1 Green Secured Railcar Equipment Notes (the "TRL-2025 Notes").
The TRL-2025 Notes bear interest at an all-in interest rate of 5.11%, are payable monthly, and have a stated final maturity date of October 19, 2055.

Net proceeds received from the railcars acquired in connection with the issuance of the TRL-2025 Notes were used to repay approximately $259.0 million of borrowings under TILC's warehouse loan facility; to redeem in full the outstanding debt of approximately $133.8 million under TRL-2010; and for general corporate purposes.
